Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Emma Kim (Redwood AE), Jose Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lydia Park (MetroFin - Head of AI), Omar Singh (MetroFin - CTO), Nina Patel (MetroFin - Security)

Auto-generated Summary (brief, may be imperfect):
Redwood gave a hosted API walkthrough covering chat and text generation basics: streaming responses, core params (temperature, max_tokens), retries and backoff, SDK and REST usage, and basic observability in the Console. Customer concerned about latency, cost tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS, and data residency. Agreed to run a short POC to benchmark latency and cost on representative prompts. Action: Emma to send pricing and security docs; Jose to prepare benchmark script.

Topics:
- Hosted API overview
- Streaming responses and chunked tokens
- Parameters: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop, presence/ frequency penalties
- Retries, idempotency keys, and rate limiting behavior
- SDK examples (node/python) and curl snippets
- Console observability and token/cost breakdowns
- Security: SOC2, KMS/Key management, data retention, SSO

Action items (auto section): see metadata action_items

Transcript:
[00:00] Emma Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Emma, I'm the AE on the account, joining today with Jose from our solutions team, uh Jose do you want to say hi?
[00:06] Jose Alvarez: Yeah hi hi, Jose Alvarez, SE. I'll be doing the demo deep dive on streaming and retries.
[00:10] Lydia Park: Hi, Lydia here. Thanks Emma. Omar and Nina are also on from our side.
[00:14] Omar Singh: Hey all.
[00:15] Nina Patel: Hi. Happy to be here.
[00:17] Emma Kim: Cool, quick agenda we have about 40 minutes, give a quick hosted API overview, then Jose will demo chat generation, streaming chunks and talk through params, then we'll go over retries, idempotency, and monitoring, and finish with Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:30] Lydia Park: Yep sounds good. We're mainly evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a customer-facing assistant, so latency and cost are top of mind. Also security and auditables.
[00:40] Emma Kim: Totally understood. We'll touch on all those.
[00:44] Jose Alvarez: Alright switching to my screen, let me pull up the Console. So Redwood's hosted API is a simple REST and SDK interface. Here's a sample chat call, we send messages, model picks up context, and you get streaming tokens back.
[01:05] Jose Alvarez: (demo) Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-2-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize Q1 performance"}],"stream":true}'
[01:22] Omar Singh: Quick Q, does stream=true open a chunked HTTP stream or SSE?
[01:27] Jose Alvarez: Good question. It's a chunked HTTP stream that yields token batches; our SDKs wrap that into async iterators. There is also an SSE option for some clients. Occasionally the transcript generator will show K-V cache as K-V cash, so apologies for typos here.
[01:40] Lydia Park: And how do we control latency vs cost?
[01:43] Jose Alvarez: Two levers: model choice and inference params. Lighter models have lower latency and cost. You can also tune temperature and max_tokens to reduce output size. In the Console we show token-level breakdown per-request so you can see where time and cost are going. Also batching and prefix caching help on high-throughput workloads.
[02:05] Jose Alvarez: Demo of parameters: temperature - controls randomness, top_p similar for nucleus sampling, max_tokens caps output length, stop sequences to truncate. Presence/frequency penalties help avoid repetition.
[02:22] Lydia Park: For repeatable outputs for assistants, we prefer low temp and explicit stop.
[02:27] Jose Alvarez: Yep that's the typical pattern.
[02:30] Jose Alvarez: Now on retries: if you get a 5xx or transient timeout we recommend exponential backoff with jitter. Use an idempotency key on create-type calls to avoid duplicate side-effects. Our SDK includes a retry helper that honors rate-limit headers.
[02:50] Nina Patel: Do you expose rate limit headers and recommended backoff windows?
[02:55] Jose Alvarez: Yes X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After — and our docs show suggested backoff multipliers. For long tails you can fallback to a cheaper model variant to reduce failure windows.
[03:10] Omar Singh: About retries creating duplicate messages: we have a couple of downstream event hooks, would idempotency be sufficient?
[03:16] Jose Alvarez: Idempotency should cover create semantics; for async workflows we recommend persist request IDs and dedupe on your side too.
[03:25] Emma Kim: I also want to note we do request-level logging and you can hook to audit logs in the Console, plus options for longer retention for enterprise plans.
[03:35] Lydia Park: On security, Nina is concerned about keys and encryption. Can you run through KMS and data retention?
[03:42] Jose Alvarez: Sure. For hosted we are SOC 2 certified, data is encrypted at rest and in transit. For customer-managed keys we support KMS integrations and HSM for Private deployments; hosted customers can opt into using a customer KMS in some regions. We keep a configurable retention window and can disable retention for certain enterprise agreements.
[04:05] Nina Patel: Do you have SSO and SCIM for user management?
[04:09] Emma Kim: Yes SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM provisioning are supported for enterprise accounts. We'll include the security whitepaper with details.
[04:16] Jose Alvarez: Back to streaming: one caveat if the connection is interrupted mid-stream you can reconnect and request the remainder using the conversation ID; the SDK does this gracefully in most cases. There's also partial aggregation in the Console.
[04:32] Lydia Park: Interesting. For latency numbers, what's typical p95 on redwood-2-small for 256 token generation?
[04:38] Jose Alvarez: For small models p95 is usually ~180-250ms per request for short sequences in our hosted regions, bigger models are higher. We'll include benchmark numbers but recommend running your own POC with your exact prompts since results vary by prompt complexity and tokenization.
[04:56] Omar Singh: Can we get a side-by-side of hosted vs dedicated latencies and costs?
[04:59] Emma Kim: Absolutely I'll include a comparison sheet. Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and lower variance but requires a commit. Hosted is faster to try.
[05:10] Jose Alvarez: Demoing SDK snippet: node example with async iterator for streaming. (snippet) const stream = client.chat.stream(...); for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk.text) }
[05:26] Jose Alvarez: Also show param tuning for safety and hallucination controls: deterministic prompts, system messages, and safety heuristics.
[05:34] Lydia Park: For content safety we have regulated financial advice concerns. Does Redwood provide moderation or safety filters?
[05:40] Jose Alvarez: We have optional moderation endpoints and content policies; you can pre-filter inputs and post-filter outputs. For regulated workflows many customers chain a lightweight classifier before showing user-facing content.
[05:52] Nina Patel: On data residency we have EU customers only we have EU regions and separate logs?
[05:58] Emma Kim: Yes we have EU regions, and audit logs and data residency controls for enterprise, will share our region map and options.
[06:08] Lydia Park: About retries again in your SDK's retry helper, what's the default max retries?
[06:12] Jose Alvarez: Default is 3 with exponential backoff and jitter, but configurable. For production we usually recommend 2-4 depending on your tolerance for added latency.
[06:22] Omar Singh: Any best practice around token limits to avoid surprise cost spikes?
[06:26] Jose Alvarez: Set max_tokens conservative, use stop sequences, and in Console set alerts on token usage. We also provide a cost forecast per-route.
[06:36] Jose Alvarez: Now I'll show the Console: per-request token breakdown, cost column, latency histogram, and token-level streamer bucket. You can filter by model, route, or user token.
[06:48] Jose Alvarez: There's also an Optimize module where we run model recommendations and quantization suggestions based on your workload; it will tell you if switching to a quantized variant or lower size model saves cost without harming quality.
[07:02] Lydia Park: Can Optimize integrate with our CI so we get regression alerts when quality drops?
[07:06] Jose Alvarez: Yes you can upload prompt sets and reference outputs, and Optimize will monitor quality and send regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[07:15] Emma Kim: Quick pause for questions.
[07:18] Lydia Park: What's the onboarding timeline for a small POC?
[07:21] Emma Kim: Usually 1-2 weeks from kickoff for a standard hosted POC Jose will provision API keys and a benchmark harness, and we can help onboard samples.
[07:30] Jose Alvarez: For benchmark harness we'll need sample prompts and expected throughput, and we'll run both latency and cost runs across 1k-5k queries.
[07:40] Omar Singh: For the POC, can you mimic our traffic patterns with bursts?
[07:44] Jose Alvarez: Yes we can simulate your traffic patterns; for hosted there are autoscaling burst behaviors and for Dedicated we can show reserved capacity profiles.
[07:54] Nina Patel: Any risks for PII exposure in logs during the POC?
[07:58] Jose Alvarez: You can opt out of retention for the POC, and for sensitive data we recommend tokenizing or masking before sending. We also offer Private deployments for air-gapped or regulated cases.
[08:10] Lydia Park: Great. A few notes our success criteria: p95 latency under 300ms for short prompts, cost under $0.0008 per 1k tokens equivalent for NLU flows, and no retention of PII. We'll share specifics.
[08:26] Emma Kim: Perfect that's helpful for sizing.
[08:29] Jose Alvarez: One more detail on retries: if you set idempotency keys they should be unique per logical request; we see customers create a UUID per user turn to dedupe.
[08:40] Omar Singh: If stream gets interrupted do you expose a resume token?
[08:44] Jose Alvarez: We surface a conversation_id and can request missing parts; it depends on the SDK but reconnections generally resume from last acked token; not all legacy SDKs do automatic resume so we'll put that in the POC checklist.
[08:58] Lydia Park: Any gotchas around streaming and mobile clients?
[09:02] Jose Alvarez: Mobile might need a heartbeat and smaller chunk sizes, also beware of cellular connections causing more reconnects client-side buffering and resume logic help.
[09:12] Emma Kim: Ok jumping ahead a bit pricing model: hosted is usage-based per-token and per-embedding units; we'll send a pricing spreadsheet with examples for your expected QPS.
[09:22] Lydia Park: For embeddings we also have a vector store, do you recommend using Redwood embeddings and external vector DBs?
[09:27] Jose Alvarez: Many customers use Redwood embeddings and store vectors in existing stores; we can also recommend vector DB partners but it's flexible.
[09:35] Omar Singh: Competitors  Did you mention OpenAI, Anthropic earlier?
[09:38] Emma Kim: Yes they came up in evaluation; we shared where Redwood focuses on production economics and observability.
[09:44] Lydia Park: Any final security certs?
[09:47] Nina Patel: (overlapping) SOC 2? ISO?
[09:49] Emma Kim: SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 are available, plus pen test reports on request. We'll attach them in the follow-up.
[09:58] Jose Alvarez: Wrapping up, quick recap: we'll run a 1-week POC, Emma sends pricing and security docs, Jose preps benchmark script, Lydia shares prompts and success criteria.
[10:10] Lydia Park: That works. Can you also include example SDK snippets for our backend engineers?
[10:14] Emma Kim: Yes will include node/python snippets and a minimal curl example.
[10:18] Omar Singh: Timeline can we start next Tuesday?
[10:21] Emma Kim: Sounds good, I'll send a calendar invite with proposed kickoff.
[10:25] Nina Patel: And we'll review the security doc asap.
[10:28] Emma Kim: Great. Thanks all. Jose any last things?
[10:31] Jose Alvarez: I'll follow up with the benchmark checklist and sample prompt set.
[10:34] Emma Kim: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.
